seoTitle: How to Find XAUUSD in TradingView (Easy Guide)
metaDescription: Learn how to search and open the correct XAUUSD gold chart in TradingView, pick the right exchange, and avoid mixing up spot, CFD, and futures symbols.
intro: XAUUSD is the ticker traders use to track gold priced against the US dollar, but TradingView lists several versions of it from different data providers. This guide walks through finding the correct XAUUSD chart, understanding what the symbol actually represents, and choosing the version that fits your trading style.

steps.heading: Understand what XAUUSD means
steps.body: XAUUSD represents the price of one troy ounce of gold quoted in US dollars. TradingView pulls this data from multiple providers, so the exact price can vary slightly between listings.

steps.heading: Search for the symbol
steps.body: Use TradingView's symbol search bar and type XAUUSD to see the available listings, including spot gold, CFD providers, and futures contracts.

steps.heading: Choose the right exchange or provider
steps.body: Compare the listed providers and pick the one that matches your broker or the data source you trust, since spreads and exact pricing differ between them.

steps.heading: Know the difference between spot, CFD, and futures
steps.body: Spot XAUUSD reflects the real-time cash market, CFD listings mirror a broker's pricing, and futures symbols track exchange-traded gold contracts with expiry dates — pick based on what you actually trade.

steps.heading: Set up your chart for analysis
steps.body: Once the correct symbol is open, apply your usual timeframe and indicators to start analyzing gold price action.

faq.question: Why do I see multiple XAUUSD charts on TradingView?
faq.answer: TradingView aggregates data from different providers and exchanges, so several XAUUSD listings appear with slightly different pricing and spreads.

faq.question: Is XAUUSD the same as gold futures?
faq.answer: No. Futures symbols track a specific contract with an expiry date, while spot XAUUSD reflects the continuous cash market price.

faq.question: Which XAUUSD chart should beginners use?
faq.answer: Beginners typically use the spot XAUUSD listing from a well-known data provider, since it closely tracks the real-time market without contract expiry complications.

faq.question: Can I trade XAUUSD directly from TradingView?
faq.answer: TradingView is primarily a charting platform, though it supports broker integrations for trading; check whether your connected broker supports XAUUSD execution.
